stories.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
stories.detail: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO on Monday in a surprise move shortly after rejecting his offer to return. It's the latest twist in the fallout from Huang's admission of an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

details.summary: President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.

stories.title: California Democrat to resign from Congress after evidence of sexual misconduct
stories.summary: Jimmy Gomez, who lost his election this month and only serving in the House until the year's end, was accused of sexual misconduct with a staff member.
stories.detail: Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”. The 19-page report from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.

California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances."

stories.title: More transparency needed on surveillance pricing, privacy commissioner says
stories.summary: Canada's privacy commissioner says people should be warned when they are being targeted by surveillance pricing.
stories.detail: Philippe Dufresne told a parliamentary committee Monday he will be developing formal guidance about how Canada's current privacy law applies to surveillance pricing.

stories.title: Minister defends not initially banning college with surging OSAP usage
stories.summary: Universities Minister Nolan Quinn this spring made six career colleges ineligible for OSAP due to what the ministry called concerns with "high-risk" admissions practices.
stories.detail: A career college with student financial aid usage that grew thousands of per cent in a few years was not one of six the Ontario government cut off in May because of the "evolving" nature of the data, the minister of colleges and universities said Monday.
